details.label: Summary
details.text: The threat for severe weather is expected to increase by early to mid afternoon with damaging wind gusts being the primary hazard. A severe thunderstorm watch is likely

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Ahead of an MCV moving through far southeast lower MI, clusters of thunderstorms have persisted this morning over northwest into west-central OH. Downstream from that convection, a corridor of relatively fewer clouds should allow for stronger daytime heating to occur this afternoon. When coupled with boundary-layer dew points in the low to mid-70s F, daytime heating is expected to erode remaining convective inhibition, with MLCAPE increasing to 1500-2500+ J/kg. That destabilization process should allow the ongoing storms to intensify by early to mid afternoon from eastern OH into western PA and northwest WV. The current IND VWP is sampling a belt of 30-40 kt westerly winds in the 1-5 km layer, which will conditionally support cold pool organization with an attendant damaging wind risk. A brief tornado is possible, though the veered low-level winds are expected to limit the magnitude of low-level shear and a resultant greater risk
